_comment: Copy to ~/.config/herdr-remote/agent-configs.json, or point HERDR_AGENT_CONFIGS at it.
This file names the endpoints a session may be started against and which of the relay's own
environment variables may supply a credential. It is the security boundary: the app can name
an alias, a model and which of these key variables to use, and nothing else. No key VALUE
belongs in this file — export the variables in the relay's own environment.
'unset' runs first. 'env' is exported verbatim. 'secrets' binds the variable the CLI wants to
the relay variables that may fill it, in offer order. 'model_var' is where an alias's model
string goes. 'kind' must be a herdr agent kind — it is checked against the start.

providers.label: AgentRouter (codex)
_note: codex reads AGENTROUTER_API_KEY under its own name, so the binding is a rotation
between two variables rather than a rename. No base URL and no model_var: codex takes
its endpoint and its model from CODEX_HOME/config.toml, so an alias here sets the
account and the key, and the model field on its row stays empty.
